## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Nimirājacariya* (Cp 6), translated by Bhikkhu Sujato as "The Conduct of King Nimi," is a canonical narrative situated in the *Cariyāpiṭaka* section of the Pali Suttas [SuttaCentral]. In a study comparing the canonical accounts of the *Cariyāpiṭaka* with the Jātaka corpus, André Bareau catalogues the text under the title *Nimi-rāja-Cariyam*, recording it as the sixth story in the collection following *Mahā-Govinda-Cariyam* and preceding *Canda-kumāra-Cariyam* [Bareau, Les récits canoniques].

According to the SuttaCentral database, modern translations of the text are available in three languages, including an English translation by Bhikkhu Sujato [SuttaCentral].

Regarding parallels and textual reuse, SuttaCentral lists no curated parallels for this text [SuttaCentral]. Likewise, automated text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus identifies no Pali-internal shared passages and no cross-language matches meeting the reporting threshold [DharmaNexus].
